name: e2-own-language-corpus-v1
status: FROZEN before any non-English inflow value was computed.
plan_section: paper3_arxiv/PLAN.md section 5.3, and its kill condition K2
epistemic_tier: TIER 1 for the non-English cells. No inflow has ever been computed on a non-English corpus in this project, and two of the three models have never been measured at all -- bloom-3b was excluded by F171's coverage floor and polyglot-ko-1.3b's tokenizer was not cached. The English cells for those two are also new. Only llm-jp's English cell is a re-measurement, and it is included as a reproduction check.
why: F171 measured Fu et al.'s inflow term on English wikitext and found endpoints sit BELOW their frequency-matched peers. Three models in the cohort have non-English modal endpoints or non-English training, and F171 excluded or lost two of them. PLAN.md section 5.3: this turns those exclusions from embarrassments into data. K2 says that if the own-language corpus REVERSES the result, F171's finding is an English artefact and the paper is about that instead.

frozen.corpora: wikimedia/wikipedia, config 20231101.{es,ja,ko}, streamed, first 20,000,000 characters of each -- the SAME size as F171's English corpus, so corpus size cannot explain a difference. English arm re-uses wikitext-103 at 20,000,000 chars exactly as F171 did.
frozen.assignment: each model is measured on its OWN language and on English, giving a 3x2 design: bigscience/bloom-3b -> es (its modal endpoint ' ciudad' is Spanish); llm-jp/llm-jp-3-1.8b -> ja; EleutherAI/polyglot-ko-1.3b -> ko (modal endpoint ' 이').
frozen.endpoint: the model's modal endpoint TOKEN ID from results/argmax_census_hardened.json, never the decoded string -- F166's rule, and F173 showed the decoded string merges different tokens across models.
frozen.estimator: identical to F171 and imported from it where possible: inflow(t) = sum_a B[a,t] with B row-normalised (Fu Corollary 1.2's term); frequency-matched control = the endpoint's inflow percentile among the 50 tokens nearest it in log-frequency. 50 is the expected value by construction.
frozen.coverage_floor: unchanged from F171: a cell is NOT DECIDABLE if the endpoint occurs fewer than 100 times in that corpus. Applied per cell, so a model can be readable in one language and not the other -- which is itself the point.

kill_conditions.K2_from_the_plan: if endpoints beat frequency-matched peers (percentile > 50) in a MAJORITY of readable own-language cells, E2 is reversed on own-language corpora, F171's result is an English artefact, and the paper is re-scoped to that. With three models, majority means 2 of 3.
kill_conditions.K2b_insufficient: if fewer than 2 own-language cells clear the coverage floor, K2 is NOT DECIDABLE and no claim is made in either direction. Two unreadable cells cannot establish an artefact or refute one.
kill_conditions.K8_english_arm_must_reproduce: llm-jp's English cell is a re-measurement of a stored F171 number (36.0). If it does not reproduce, the pipeline has drifted and every number in this run is void -- reported as a failure of the run, not as a finding about language.
kill_conditions.K9_size_matched: any difference between a model's own-language and English cells must not be attributable to corpus size, which is why both are 20,000,000 characters. If a corpus yields fewer characters than requested, the shortfall is reported and that cell is marked size-mismatched.

refusals_recorded_before_numbers: no p-value: three models, and the cells are not independent tests of one another
no claim that a single language generalises to 'non-English'
no re-scoping of the paper on this run alone -- K2 firing is a trigger to re-scope deliberately, not a licence to rewrite the thesis inside a results file

no comparison of inflow VALUES across corpora: they are computed over different vocabularies and different texts, so only the frequency-matched PERCENTILE is comparable, and that is the only quantity compared
what_this_cannot_settle: Whether the direction holds for these languages generally. One corpus per language, one encyclopedic register, one model each. Wikipedia is not a sample of a language.
